data.title: Jaguar Health sets 1-for-15 reverse stock split; shares crash
data.description:
• Jaguar Health (JAGX) announced on Tuesday that it will execute a 1-for-15 reverse stock split on September 17, 2026, to support compliance with Nasdaq listing requirements.
  • The stock will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis when the market opens on September 17 and will continue trading under the JAGX ticker on Nasdaq.
  • Under the split, every 15 existing shares will become 1 share, with no change to the stock’s par value per share.
  • No fractional shares will be issued. Investors entitled to a fractional share will receive cash in lieu.
  • On the market side, the stock crashed almost 10% at ~$0.29 in the pre-market hours.

data.title: Goldman's Panic Index logged third-largest daily drop in 3 years
data.description:
A sudden three-point drop in the Goldman Sachs Panic Index on Friday wiped out broad market fear, registering as the third-largest single-day decline in the past three years.

The collapse in panic left markets entering the weekend with much less fear priced into broader indexes (SPY) (DIA) (QQQ), alongside continued market dispersion and recently rebuilt long positions in the tech sector (XLK). With generalized anxiety fading, investor attention shifted toward emerging headlines surrounding artificial intelligence (AIQ) and the Middle East war.

Broad market volatility also remained muted, with the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) staying well under 20 and sitting at roughly 16.90 at the time of writing.

Meanwhile, major stock indexes are extending last week's losses so far this week due to a mix of tech sector drops, energy spikes and bond market pressures. AI and chipmaker (SMH) (SOXX) shares retreated after prominent tech CEOs called for a slowdown and tighter pacing in AI development. Elsewhere, crude oil (USO) (BNO) prices climbed further above $100 a barrel after Middle East attacks and critical pipeline shutdowns in Saudi Arabia worsened supply fears. Adding to the market strain, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield (US10Y) hit the key 5% threshold ahead of a Federal Reserve decision on Wednesday, which is largely expected to feature a rate hike.

data.title: Tredegar announces CFO appointment
data.description:
• Tredegar (TG) announced that Cindy Yao will join the company as vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer, effective September 21, 2026.

  • Prior to joining Tredegar, she served as CFO of Holon Health, HF Foods Group.

data.title: American Express launches new high-yield business savings account
data.description:
American Express (AXP) on Tuesday announced the launch of a new high-yield business savings account, which lets businesses earn more on deposits and manage more finances in one place.

Features include a high annual percentage yield of 2.95%, the ability to make and receive transfers online, instant transfers to and from an American Express Business Checking account with no transfer fee, integration with accounting software and bank linkages, and 24/7 support.

The launch comes after an Amex survey found that 82% of businesses agree their excess cash could be put to better use in a savings account.

data.title: Etsy's AI search wins over shoppers -- Oppenheimer
data.description:
Product improvements, improved search results, and a strong competitive moat earned Etsy (ETSY) an upgrade to Outperform from Perform at Oppenheimer with a $90 price target that represents 21% upside to Monday’s closing price.

A survey of 2,500 U.S. consumers indicated that product improvements are working with less dependence on Google Search (GOOG) (GOOGL) and more on AI. Accordingly, this led Oppenheimer’s Jason Helfstein to raise his FY26 gross merchandise sales (GMS) estimate to a street high of 1% and 5% GMS growth in FY27 and FY28. This includes the anticipated share loss within the online handmade market from new entrants.

Oppenheimer forecasts the global online handmade market growing 9% annually between 2025 and 2028 and sees Etsy (ETSY) losing 117-135 basis points of share in 2027/2028 as the market expands. However, this limits the analysis to handmade, which was 73% of Oppenheimer’s survey, while product selection covers a much broader selection.  

The improvements to Etsy’s (ETSY) platform and AI search capabilities have not gone unnoticed by consumers, Helfstein notes, with survey results indicating 65% of consumers polled are “very” or “somewhat” likely to purchase an item. The survey results also showed 73% of buyers purchased handcrafted or made-to-order items, and 88% went directly to the website/app rather than use Google Search.

Seeking Alpha authors and Wall Street analysts both maintain a Buy rating for Etsy (ETSY), as well as Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating with a score of 3.95 out of 5.

Etsy (ETSY) shares are more than 3% higher in Tuesday’s premarket with a year-to-date gain of 34% vs. 11% for the benchmark S&P index.

data.title: TSMC treads carefully on AI, calling it a ‘three-year-old superman’
data.description:
A senior Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) executive compared artificial intelligence to a toddler with extraordinary powers, highlighting the company’s cautious approach to deploying the technology, particularly when sensitive information is involved.

TSMC co-chief operating officer Y.J. Mii said Tuesday that the company is wary of using AI with confidential research and development data because improper use could result in information leaks or data loss. He pointed to recent cases involving OpenAI (OPENAI) and Anthropic (ANTHRO) models infiltrating external organizations.

“AI is like a three-year old superman. It can be quite powerful, but it doesn’t know what kind of damage it can inflict,” Mii told students at National Taiwan University, his alma mater. “And it doesn’t know right from wrong,” he said, without elaborating.

Mii made the comments during a career forum in Taipei while answering questions about workplace AI adoption. His remarks come after incidents involving rogue AI agents accessing Hugging Face and other data systems, fueling debate over whether the industry should slow AI development to give safety measures time to catch up.

Mii didn’t comment at length about the debate over the broader dangers of AI to humanity but focused more on the technology’s impracticality for applications such as cutting-edge chip design.

He said the technology currently offers limited help in developing next-generation chipmaking processes, where progress depends more on physical constraints and the availability of capable manufacturing equipment.

For TSMC, protecting proprietary technology remains a priority as the company benefits from surging demand for AI chips from customers, including Nvidia (NVDA) and Apple (AAPL).

data.title: Capstone Energy+ boosts New Mexico's gas power fleet to 12 MW
data.description:
• Capstone Energy+ (CEPL) announced on Tuesday that it delivered 2 additional MW of C1000S gas turbines to support a major U.S. midstream natural gas project in southern New Mexico.
  • The expansion brings the customer’s fleet to 12 C1000S systems, providing 12 MW of on-site power across 6 interconnected gas facilities.
  • The project began in 2024 with 8 rental units and has since expanded to 12 units through purchases and additions.
  • Moreover, the project supports remote compressor stations across 200K+ acres and 200 miles of pipelines, where utility power is unavailable.
  • The company said the latest expansion highlights demand for its low-maintenance, low-emissions, and reliable distributed power systems in critical energy infrastructure.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: New York Times upgraded to Buy at Guggenheim on digital growth, valuation
data.description:
Guggenheim upgraded The New York Times Company (NYT) to Buy from Neutral and raised its price target to $82 from $70, citing a more attractive valuation and confidence in sustained digital advertising and subscription growth.

New PT represents about 16.6% upside from the stock's last close.

Analyst Michael Morris and team said the company can sustain “low-double digit digital advertising growth” through 2027 despite tougher comparisons, citing strong demand across its News, Sports, Games, and Shopping properties, as well as additional inventory and video monetization opportunities.

Morris expects digital subscriptions to grow about 10% next year, supported by higher average revenue per user and more than 1.09 million net additions. It said the company has “enough levers to pull” to sustain ARPU growth despite a tough comparison following a $5 price increase for its most tenured bundled subscribers this year.

Operating expenses are also expected to normalize to “mid-single digit” growth as the company laps investments in video and newsroom initiatives, though elevated sales and marketing spending remains a concern.

The brokerage raised its 2027 adjusted operating profit forecast to $714 million from $682 million, above the consensus of $699 million, and said NYT’s valuation now offers an “attractive entry point.”

Shares edged about 1.5% higher in the premarket trading on Tuesday.

data.title: Honeywell upgrades Marine Corps security; labor cost seen down 80%
data.description:
• Honeywell Technologies (HON) announced on Tuesday that it successfully deployed its LenelS2 OnGuard access control system for the U.S. Marine Corps, supporting its Barracks 2030 modernization initiative.
  • The platform enables remote management of access permissions and activity monitoring across participating barracks, replacing fragmented legacy systems.
  • The platform is designed to support more than 70K locks across Marine Corps installations.
  • The modernization effort is estimated to reduce labor costs by ~80% and material costs by 60% compared with legacy systems.
  • The pilot at Marine Corps Air Station Beaufort, South Carolina, met its objectives ahead of schedule, paving the way for expansion to additional locations.
  • The deployment strengthens Honeywell’s position in large-scale government security and access control projects.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Algorhythm announces CEO departure
data.description:
Algorhythm (RIME) announced on Tuesday an evaluation of strategic alternatives and a corporate repositioning.

As part of the transition, the company dismissed Gary Atkinson as chief executive officer, following approximately 20 years of service. Atkinson also resigned from the company’s board of directors.

“I want to take this opportunity to thank the many employees, business partners, customers, and shareholders who have supported the Company throughout my time here,” said Gary Atkinson. “I am proud of what our team has accomplished together and believe we have positioned Algorhythm for an exciting new chapter.”

“This transition was part of a deliberate process by the Company to position itself for its next phase of growth,” continued Atkinson. “I am excited about the opportunities being pursued by the Company and believe the new leadership team brings a compelling vision for its future. As a continuing shareholder, I look forward to watching that strategy take shape in the coming weeks and months.”

Shares of RIME gained more than 5% pre-market. 

Source: press release
